name: Reading the API
description: Learn how to read the generated API reference: the parts, the inline list, a filter, one prop and its event, the slots, and the hover card.

steps.title: API Reference
steps.task: Every component page ends here. This block is generated from the source. It is not a hand-written table.
steps.hint: Composable pages end with the same kind of block. Theirs lists functions, options, properties, and methods instead of props, events, and slots.
steps.learn: Find the generated reference on a component page

steps.title: One card per part
steps.task: Tabs is a compound. Each card is one part: Root, List, Item, and Panel, with its own props, events, and slots.
steps.hint: The line under a name is a count, not a summary. It always includes props. Events and slots appear only when that part has them.
steps.learn: Read a compound as separate parts

steps.title: Open it here
steps.task: We opened the reference on this page. Show inline expands every part in place. The link cards were only the index.
steps.hint: Show inline is also a switch in the page settings, so you can leave every component page expanded. This tour puts your previous choice back when it ends.

steps.title: Filter the page
steps.task: We typed model. The filter matches names and descriptions on this page only. It does not search the rest of the docs.
steps.hint: A part name such as Item shows that part in full, and a word from a description matches too. Case does not matter, and clearing the field brings every part back.

steps.title: Props
steps.task: We cleared the filter. This is the props list for Tabs.Root. Every prop on this part is a row in this list.
steps.hint: The name, the type, the description, and the default, when there is one, all sit on that row. Events and slots for the same part follow below.

steps.title: One prop
steps.task: modelValue is the active tab. The only thing under the name is the type: T, a list of T, or undefined.
steps.hint: Bind it with v-model. This row has no default chip. Whether a tab starts selected is the next prop, mandatory.

steps.title: The default
steps.task: mandatory decides whether a tab has to stay selected. The default on this row is force, which selects the first tab that is not disabled.
steps.hint: Read the default together with the description. false means nothing is forced, true keeps the last selected tab, and force picks one for you.
steps.learn: Use a prop's default and its description together

steps.title: The event
steps.task: update:model-value fires when the selected tab changes. v-model is modelValue plus this event, so you usually do not listen to it yourself.
steps.hint: The payload is the new value, the same type as modelValue. Listen here when you need the change without binding the prop.

steps.title: Slots
steps.task: Tabs.Item's slot gives you isSelected, isDisabled, and attrs. attrs already contains onClick. Bind attrs to your own element only when the item is renderless. Binding them onto a child of the default button fires the click twice.
steps.hint: The item renders a button unless it is renderless. On that button, attrs is already applied, including onClick, so a click on a child runs both.
steps.learn: Read slot props and know when to bind attrs

steps.title: Hover a name
steps.task: We hovered Tabs.Root in the page. The card is the same reference: props, a docs link, and the API page.
steps.hint: The card opens for names this site recognizes, and it shows the same props you just read, plus a docs link and the API page. Other code on the page stays plain.
steps.learn: Open the reference from a name in the prose

steps.title: Same data, own page
steps.task: The label says View standalone. It closes this list and shows the part cards again. Those cards open the same reference on its own page.
steps.hint: The page for Tabs is /api/tabs. A card takes you there. This button only brings the cards back.

steps.title: That's the reference
steps.task: Cards for the parts, inline for the details, hover when a name shows up in the prose.
steps.hint: Composable pages use the same layout. You will see functions, options, properties, and methods in place of props, events, and slots.
steps.learn: Read an API reference without hunting
